title: "Figure 6 — where MacroIR stops being calibrated, and why"

<!--
RENUMBERED 2026-08-10: this figure is now FIGURE 6. It was Figure 5 until the tau_int decision
panel (figure_5.Rmd) was promoted into the body ahead of it; the usage map moved to Figure 7.

WHAT THIS FIGURE IS FOR. Figure 4 shows IR's panels nearly blank, which raises the question the
abstract already answers in words: the boundary-conditioned filter is calibrated over most of the
sweep, "departing toward few channels and low noise, where the Gaussian closure is misspecified".
Figure 7 then uses that departure as the region-0 boundary of the usage map. Nothing between them
shows the data. This figure is that evidence, and it is the only place in the paper where the
threshold in `05_discussion.tex` ([THRESHOLD-DJ]) can be read off.

WHY IT CANNOT BE PART OF FIGURE 4. On Figure 4's shared scale, clipped at 10^+-3, a factor 1.46 is
a faint tint. The departure lives between 0.6 and 1.6 and needs an axis, not a colour.

THE LAYOUT. Each block is a design-plane grid in the same orientation as Figures 4 and 7: N_ch
increases to the right, instrumental noise increases upward, and inside every cell the horizontal
axis is the sampling interval. The three blocks are the distortion and its two causes, so the
figure says where, how much, with what confidence, and why, on one page.

SAMPLING. N_ch runs in ~0.65-decade steps against noise in ~0.3-decade steps. That is not
arbitrary: the region-0 boundary of Figure 7 has a fitted slope of -0.56 in
dlog10(noise)/dlog10(N_ch), so a decade of channels trades against ~0.56 decades of noise and the
noise axis needs about twice the resolution to sample the field evenly.

ANCHOR AND FAMILY, and why this differs from figures/in_progress/figure_5_distortion_lines_bynch.Rmd,
which is where this figure started. That draft reads data/433ed13, which holds no `_G` files, so it
necessarily used `Probit_statistics_Likelihood_Information_Distortion` (the numerical Fisher) at
theta_sim. This one uses the SAME quantity and anchor as Figure 4: the Gaussian information
distortion at the pooled optimum, via figure_4_common.R's `stat`. The two agree in shape and
magnitude (k_off ~1.4 vs 1.46 at N_ch 10, lowest noise), so this is a consistency fix and not a
change of result. See 03_diagnostics.tex: the Gaussian Fisher is the anchor by design.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# figure_4_common.R filters N_ch to the four decades Figure 4 maps. This figure needs the fine
# ladder that exists on disk (10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000), so NCHS is
# widened in memory. The file on disk is NOT modified: Figure 4's own byNch height is computed as
# a sum over NCHS, so widening it there would silently change that figure.
src <- readLines("figure_4_common.R")
i <- grep("^NCHS *<-", src)
stopifnot(length(i) == 1)
src[i] <- "NCHS <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000)"
eval(parse(text = src), envir = globalenv())
```

```{r constants}
ERR_MAX <- 0.2          # drop points whose bootstrap half-width exceeds this: unreliable, not news
# ...but it must never drop anything silently. On the freeze it fires on zero points (median
# half-width 0.03 across the grid); it is kept as a guard for re-runs on noisier data, and the
# count is printed so a future reader can see whether it started biting.
PL   <- c(off = "k[off]", Num_ch_mean = "N[ch]")
# Okabe-Ito. The two parameters and the reference line are mutually distinguishable for every kind
# of colour blindness, and NUL is the green figure_3.Rmd already uses for the expected value.
PCOL <- c("k[off]" = "#0072B2", "N[ch]" = "#E69F00")
NUL  <- "#009E73"
NCH  <- c(10, 50, 200, 1000)                      # ~0.65-decade steps; see the header
NZ   <- c(0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 1)        # dimensionless noise = swept label / 10
CMP  <- c(total = "A   total", sample = "B   per-sample", corr = "C   correlation")
YW   <- 0.32            # width the y axis and its title take, in column units (measured)

# ONE y range for every block. Each component is split into two sub-blocks and each block is its
# own ggplot, so without explicit limits every one computes its own range from its own data: the
# N_ch = 10 column, which has the widest data, got a stretched axis and its reference line at 1
# sat at a different height from its neighbours'. The columns are meant to be compared, so the
# range is computed once over everything that will be drawn and imposed on all of them.
.pl <- stat %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo == "macro_IR", param %in% names(PL), Num_ch %in% NCH,
                comp %in% names(CMP)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(zz = as.numeric(noise) / 10) %>%
  dplyr::filter(zz %in% NZ, is.finite(lo), is.finite(hi), (hi - lo) / 2 <= ERR_MAX)
YLIM <- c(min(.pl$lo, na.rm = TRUE) / 1.03, max(.pl$hi, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.03)
.all <- stat %>%
  dplyr::filter(algo == "macro_IR", param %in% names(PL), Num_ch %in% NCH,
                comp %in% names(CMP)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(zz = as.numeric(noise) / 10) %>% dplyr::filter(zz %in% NZ)
cat(sprintf("shared y range: %.3f to %.3f | ERR_MAX dropped %d of %d points\n",
            YLIM[1], YLIM[2], nrow(.all) - nrow(.pl), nrow(.all)))
```

```{r block-fn}
# One block of the grid. `nch` is the subset of channel counts it draws: each component is split
# into its first column and the rest, purely so the x tick labels appear once per component
# instead of four times. `first` carries the y axis, `last` the noise strip.
blk <- function(cmp, nch, first, last, xlab) {
  d <- stat %>%
    dplyr::filter(algo == "macro_IR", param %in% names(PL), Num_ch %in% nch, comp == cmp) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(zz = as.numeric(noise) / 10) %>%
    dplyr::filter(zz %in% NZ, is.finite(lo), is.finite(hi), (hi - lo) / 2 <= ERR_MAX)
  nl <- sort(unique(d$Num_ch)); zl <- sort(unique(d$zz), decreasing = TRUE)
  # every first-row strip carries two lines so the three blocks' header rows align; only the
  # leftmost block spells the variable name out
  nlab <- sprintf('atop("%s", "%s")', ifelse(first & seq_along(nl) == 1, "N_ch", ""), nl)
  zlab <- format(zl, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE)
  zlab <- sprintf('atop("%s", "%s")', ifelse(last & seq_along(zl) == 1, "noise", ""), zlab)
  d <- d %>% dplyr::mutate(pf   = factor(PL[param], levels = PL),
                           nchf = factor(Num_ch, levels = nl, labels = nlab),
                           nzf  = factor(zz, levels = zl, labels = zlab))
  # `m` (the bootstrap mean), NOT `Dconf`: the latter is the conservative CI edge collapsed
  # to 1 wherever the interval brackets it (figure_4_common.R:200), which is right for colouring a
  # map and wrong for a line, where it would ride the edge of the band drawn beside it.
  ggplot(d, aes(interval_in_tau, m, colour = pf, group = pf)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = NUL, linewidth = .35) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = pf), colour = NA, alpha = .28) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .45) +
    facet_grid(nzf ~ nchf, labeller = label_parsed) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(.01, 1), labels = if (xlab) c("0.01", "1") else c("", "")) +
    scale_y_log10(breaks = c(.6, 1, 1.5), limits = YLIM) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PCOL, labels = parse(text = PL), name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PCOL, guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = if (first) "distortion factor" else NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(.04, "cm"),
          legend.position = "none",
          axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
          axis.text.y  = if (first) element_text(size = 7) else element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = if (first) element_line() else element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = if (first) element_text(size = 8) else element_blank(),
          strip.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
          strip.text.y = if (last) element_text(size = 7, angle = 0) else element_blank(),
          # the two sub-blocks of a component are one grid, so the seam between them is closed
          plot.margin  = if (xlab) margin(2, 0, 2, 1) else margin(2, 1, 2, 0))
}

txt <- function(s, sz = 8, bold = FALSE, left = FALSE) ggplot() +
  theme_void(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  annotate("text", x = if (left) 0.02 else .5, y = .5, label = s, size = sz * 0.3527,
           hjust = if (left) 0 else .5, fontface = if (bold) "bold" else "plain") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off")
```

```{r assemble}
ks <- names(CMP)
cs <- lapply(seq_along(ks), function(j) {
  first <- j == 1; last <- j == length(ks)
  list(blk(ks[j], NCH[1],  first = first, last = FALSE, xlab = TRUE),
       blk(ks[j], NCH[-1], first = FALSE, last = last,  xlab = FALSE))
})
plots <- list(); ws <- numeric(0); cw <- numeric(0)
for (j in seq_along(cs)) {
  w1 <- 1 + if (j == 1) YW else 0
  if (j > 1) { plots <- c(plots, list(plot_spacer())); ws <- c(ws, .18) }
  plots <- c(plots, list(cs[[j]][[1]], cs[[j]][[2]]))
  ws <- c(ws, w1, length(NCH) - 1)
  cw <- c(cw, w1 + length(NCH) - 1)
}
row <- wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1, widths = ws)

tt <- list(); tw <- numeric(0)
for (j in seq_along(cs)) {
  if (j > 1) { tt <- c(tt, list(plot_spacer())); tw <- c(tw, .18) }
  tt <- c(tt, list(txt(unname(CMP[j]), bold = TRUE, left = TRUE))); tw <- c(tw, cw[j])
}
ttl <- wrap_plots(tt, nrow = 1, widths = tw)

# colour key at the foot, where Figure 4 puts its colour bars
key <- ggplot(data.frame(x = 1:2, y = 1, p = factor(names(PCOL), levels = names(PCOL))),
              aes(x, y, colour = p)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = p), linewidth = .6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = PCOL, labels = parse(text = PL), name = NULL) +
  theme_void(base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.width = unit(16, "pt"), legend.box.spacing = unit(0, "pt"))

g <- ttl / row / txt("dimensionless sampling interval") / key +
  plot_layout(heights = c(0.14, 4.4, 0.13, 0.16))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 4.83}
g
ggsave("Figure_6.pdf", g, width = 7.4, height = 4.83)
cat("Figure_6.pdf: 7.40 x 4.83 in;",
    "N_ch", paste(NCH, collapse = ","), "x noise", length(NZ), "x three components\n")
```
